transcript:
Meeting header:
Title: ZenithLane UAT & Marketplace Connector integration review
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Clarke (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maria Lopez (ZenithLane CTO), Anil Kapoor (Platform Lead), Devika Sharma (Security), Tom Reyes (SRE), Jia Chen (QA)

Summary:
Quick sync to validate marketplace packaging approach for Redwood Connector, confirm UAT scope and test data, and run through security/compliance questions for the on-prem connector listing. Action items around compatibility tests, packaging checklist, and scheduling pilot.

Topics:
- Marketplace packaging (container image, helm chart, marketplace shim)
- Private / on-prem connector behavior (VPC, CNI, service mesh issues)
- Security: KMS/HSM, SSO, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
- UAT acceptance criteria and performance benchmarks
- Next steps and pilot scheduling

Action items (captured): see metadata

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: all right everyone thanks for joining. this is Sophie from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we wanted to make sure we had the right folks from Zenith Lane for the marketplace connector and the on prem packaging review.
[00:23] Maria: yep, this is Maria, thanks. we got Anil, Devika, Tom and Jia on the line. ready to go.
[00:30] Ethan: hi hi, Ethan here - SE. quick agenda: packaging checklist, integration touchpoints, compatibility tests, and security ask. hope that works.
[00:45] Anil: sounds good. we're mainly focused on two things: the marketplace listing for our internal customers and the UAT for the on-prem connector that plugs into our CNI and service mesh.
[01:05] Sophie: perfect. Priya from my team is going to jump in on the helm / chart specifics.
[01:12] Priya: hey all - quick note: Redwood's marketplace packaging is a small shim that wraps the runtime image plus a helm chart. we typically provide a reference manifest and a marketplace listing artifact. for private deployments we also provide a VPC-enabled bundle.
[01:35] Devika: can you clarify what you mean by "shim"? in our security review last week we flagged any extra binary or sidecar as needing code review and verification.
[01:47] Priya: sure, by shim i mean a lightweight startup wrapper that does license handshake and marketplace metering callbacks. it's a container entrypoint, not a binary with heavy logic. but yes, understandable for security. we can provide source and reproducible build proofs.
[02:09] Jia: for UAT we need to know how to seed data and how to stub telemetry so we don't hit production metering. can you confirm a local-only mode?
[02:21] Ethan: yes, we do a local sandbox config that disables outbound metering and hooks into a test KMS if desired. we usually ship a sample values.yaml for helm that toggles sandbox=true.
[02:35] Tom: our cluster uses a custom CNI (Calico fork) plus Istio service mesh. any known issues with sidecars or with the KV cache behavior when running through mesh?
[02:49] Ethan: good question. we had one customer with Istio where initial connection timeouts happened because mesh mTLS settings required additional policies. our recommendation is to annotate the pod to bypass sidecar injection for the lightweight "shim", or inject the "shim" as a sidecar compatible with mesh - depends on your security stance. note: sometimes the KV cache persistency looked like a KV "cash" in logs — occasional mis-typed logs we had to fix.
[03:16] Anil: ok so bypass injection is acceptable for the connector itself, but our platform team prefers everything in mesh. what's the risk profile?
[03:26] Ethan: if you put the connector behind mesh, you need to ensure the kernel-level parameters for gRPC keepalives are tuned; we saw stalls at long sequences without keepalive tweaks. also watch for headless svc DNS resolution with the mesh sidecars.
[03:44] Maria: from a product standpoint, we need the marketplace listing to show a one-click deploy for internal teams. what's required from our side to meet store policies?
[03:56] Sophie: typically the marketplace requires: signed container images, an attestation of the provenance (reproducible build), a Helm chart with parameterized values, a README and support contact, and a compatibility matrix. we'll send our packaging checklist.
[04:13] Devika: on encryption - we need to confirm KMS integration and HSM options. does Redwood support using customer's KMS keys for model cache and logs?
[04:26] Priya: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM. for the connector we can configure keywrap with your KMS, we'll provide steps for Key rotation. small caveat: for on-prem air-gapped, we have a local keystore mode but that requires separate compliance attestation.
[04:48] Devika: air-gap mode? that would need SOC2 attestation and additional paperwork. is that offered as part of the listing?
[04:57] Sophie: it's an add-on for private deployments. for the marketplace listing itself, we call out supported modes (hosted, dedicated, private). air-gap is listed under "private/on-prem - contact sales". we'll include a compliance checklist and SOC2/ISO artifacts references.
[05:20] Jia: about the UAT data - can you provide a synthetic dataset generator or do we need to create logs ourselves?
[05:29] Ethan: we have a small repo with synthetic prompts and a replay harness that can simulate typical traffic patterns including sequence length distributions. we'll hand that over. the harness can simulate KV cache pressure and high concurrency.
[05:44] Anil: performance expectations — what latency numbers should we benchmark against in UAT?
[05:50] Priya: depends on model variant. for the common open LLM we recommend testing 512-token sequences at p95 latency targets: hosted ~180-220ms, dedicated ~120-160ms on p4-equivalent, private depends on local GPU. for on-prem with mixed CPUs/GPUs you'll see variance.
[06:12] Maria: we have A100s in our lab. will that map to your recommended dedicated numbers?
[06:18] Ethan: A100 should be favorable — similar to our p4 estimates for many models. but quantization and kernel selection matter. we'll help run microbenchmarks during pilot.
[06:32] Tom: do you have a sizing guide? our infra owner wants exact vCPU, memory, and GPU counts per throughput.
[06:39] Priya: yes, we'll share the sizing guide and a calculator sheet. it includes throughput per GPU and token/s estimates.
[06:46] Maria: security again — audit logs and RBAC: we need per-tenant audit trails and the ability to purge PII on demand. can Redwood do object-level purge and provide chain-of-custody?
[06:59] Ethan: Redwood Private surfaces audit logs and supports per-tenant log segregation. purge workflows exist but require KMS integration to render data unrecoverable. chain-of-custody can be documented via our audit export. we'll attach an example log schema.
[07:20] Devika: about SSO - we use Okta and support SAML/OIDC. do you support delegated identity for the connector so calls to model endpoints carry our principal?
[07:31] Sophie: we support SAML for the console and OIDC for service-to-service. for the connector, you can propagate a tenant token and we accept signed JWTs if set up with our trust anchor. we'll provide config examples.
[07:47] Tom: on the helm side, we need to override limits and run as non-root - any constraints?
[07:56] Priya: charts support podSecurityContext, nonRoot, and you can set resource limits. the only part that needs elevated privileges is optional hostPath mounting for packed cache; but there are workarounds using ephemeral volumes. we'll annotate those in the values.yaml.
[08:17] Anil: network egress - the connector phones home for metering and license checks; can that be locked down to a fixed IP range we can firewall to?
[08:27] Ethan: yes, we have an IP range for marketplace callbacks and we can provide TLS pinned certs or a static peering option for dedicated/private deployments. for air-gapped you'll use the local license server mode.
[08:41] Maria: what's the vulnerability scanning policy for the images listed in the marketplace?
[08:48] Priya: images go through CVE scanning with weekly scans. we publish SBOMs (software bill of materials) for each release. the marketplace requires SBOM and a vulnerability statement.
[09:02] Jia: QA question: will the marketplace flow allow us to deploy with custom values, like enabling our own logging endpoint?
[09:11] Sophie: yes, values.yaml exposes logging endpoint, telemetry toggles, and sampling rates. it's parameterized.
[09:20] Devika: regulatory: we have EU customers; does your marketplace listing allow regional images or regional repositories so EU nodes don't pull from non-EU registries?
[09:33] Priya: we can publish region-specific references and recommend using a registry mirror in EU for data residency. the listing metadata can include region tags.
[09:43] Anil: one technical worry: our service mesh injects proxy sidecars that rewrite cluster DNS, and we saw gRPC timeouts previously. any tuning suggestions?
[09:55] Ethan: configure gRPC keepalives, increase maxConcurrentStreams in the proxy, and ensure HTTP/2 settings are aligned. we can provide a tuning doc from another customer who had Istio + mTLS on.
[10:12] Maria: can we talk about packaging timeline? we want the listing live internally by end of August. is that realistic?
[10:22] Sophie: yes, for an internal listing that should be achievable: week 1 - packaging & checklist; week 2 - UAT + compatibility tests; week 3 - pilot and fixups; week 4 - internal rollout. so target late August is reasonable.
[10:36] Jia: UAT acceptance criteria - we need p95 latency under X, zero functional regressions vs baseline, and successful shutdown/start cycles. can we align a checklist?
[10:46] Ethan: yes we'll draft an acceptance checklist and include the synthetic harness. include perf targets per model variant.
[10:54] Devika: license metering: what data is sent in callbacks? PII concerns?
[10:59] Priya: metering only sends aggregated token counts and license IDs. no PII by default. for extra caution you can enable redaction in the connector.
[11:12] Tom: about the on-prem runtime - do you provide pre-built RPMs or just container images?
[11:19] Sophie: primarily container images; we can provide packaging recipes for distros upon request. marketplace flow is container-first.
[11:27] Anil: our compliance team will want to run a pen-test on the connector. typical engagement length?
[11:34] Ethan: most pen-tests for a connector run 2-3 weeks, and we supply a mitigation backlog template. we also share recent third-party test summaries.
[11:46] Maria: what about upgrade paths? if we publish in marketplace and later push a minor patch, how does upgrade happen?
[11:55] Priya: helm upgrades with canary flags supported. marketplace-level upgrades can be automated or manual; we'll document recommended rollout - canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback hooks.
[12:11] Jia: rewind - sample test data - can that include long tails so we exercise large context windows?
[12:18] Ethan: yes the harness includes a distribution file; you can tweak percentile of long sequences to simulate TTLs.
[12:27] Devika: auditing - do you provide signed audit exports so we can feed into our SIEM?
[12:34] Sophie: yes, logs can be signed and exported to S3 or your syslog endpoints; schema will be provided.
[12:43] Anil: any blockers you foresee for our environment?
[12:46] Ethan: main risks are CNI compatibility and Istio mTLS settings; both are solvable with sidecar annotations and keepalive tuning. also the local KMS mode requires coordination for key custody.
[13:00] Maria: ok let's go through a quick checklist of things we'll need from Redwood and what you need from us.
[13:08] Sophie: from Redwood: packaging checklist, SBOMs, sample values.yaml, synthetic harness, sizing guide, compatibility test results.
[13:18] Maria: from ZenithLane: UAT acceptance doc, sample dataset, list of cluster variants (CNI/mesh versions), contact for infra to run tests.
[13:28] Tom: i can be the infra contact for running the tests.
[13:30] Sophie: great. any questions on pricing? do you want a ballpark estimate for marketplace listing vs private package?
[13:39] Maria: yes ballpark would help for budgeting.
[13:43] Sophie: we'll send a pricing matrix. for marketplace it's typically usage-based with a small listing fee; private deployments have reserved capacity or license options.
[13:53] Anil: one more thing on metrics — we want higher fidelity token-level telemetry for internal billing. is that available?
[14:02] Ethan: yes, token-level telemetry is available as an opt-in. note that increases telemetry footprint. we can set sampling or aggregate rates to reduce cost.
[14:16] Devika: re: SOC2 artifacts - can we get a redacted report?
[14:21] Sophie: yes, we have SOC2 Type II summary and an artifacts pack for partners under NDA. we'll coordinate with legal to share.
[14:33] Maria: let's hit the UAT specifics: Jia, what test cases you need?
[14:38] Jia: functional, upgrade/rollback, load at 1k concurrent sessions, and disk pressure scenarios for local cache. also chaos test for pod restarts.
[14:47] Ethan: got it, harness supports concurrent session simulation and disk pressure. we'll add restart scenarios to the test plan.
[14:58] Anil: compatibility tests timeline?
[15:01] Ethan: i can run a set of automated compat checks within 3 business days, and a deeper integration pass in ~10 days.
[15:10] Sophie: so action: Ethan runs compat by 2026-07-20. Sophie to send packaging checklist today. Maria to share UAT doc by 2026-07-21.
[15:23] Maria: noted. about the marketplace listing UI, can we preview how our brand will show?
[15:30] Priya: yes, we can share a mock listing page and metadata fields: logo, short blurb, support contact, region tags.
[15:39] Tom: for on-prem air-gapped mode, what telemetry remains?
[15:44] Ethan: none by default; you can run with local-only telemetry and export logs post-facto. metering will be local and can be uploaded via an offline attestation.
[15:57] Devika: we will want to run a mini security review on the shim source. will you provide a build reproducibility guide?
[16:05] Priya: yes, we have reproducible build docs and a binary provenance proof.
[16:12] Jia: acceptance criteria: besides perf, we need correct handling of partial responses and streaming fallback. does connector support streaming APIs?
[16:22] Ethan: yes streaming response and function calling are supported; fallback to sync mode is available for older environments.
[16:33] Maria: okay i'm comfortable with the plan. are there any particular test data privacy constraints we should be aware of?
[16:41] Sophie: avoid real customer PII in UAT. use redacted/synthetic. we'll provide a generator.
[16:48] Anil: final question - SLA for private vs marketplace listing - how are those communicated?
[16:54] Sophie: marketplace listing comes with standard support; Dedicated/Private can be covered by reserved capacity with SLA add-ons. we'll include SLA language in the package.
[17:06] Maria: excellent. let's recap next steps.
[17:10] Sophie: recap: Ethan compatibility tests (due 7/20); Sophie send packaging & pricing (due 7/16); Redwood share synthetic harness and sizing guide (7/16); Maria share UAT doc & sample data (7/21); schedule pilot week of 7/27.
[17:27] Tom: i'll prep the lab for the week of 7/27.
[17:30] Jia: i'll coordinate with Tom and create the QA checklist.
[17:34] Devika: i'll collate the SOC2 questions and share by 7/18.
[17:38] Maria: thanks everyone, this was very productive.
[17:41] Sophie: thanks all. we'll follow up with the checklist and prices.
[17:45] [Meeting end]
